entries.title: Five killed as Russia launches fresh aerial attacks across Ukraine
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accuses Russia of targeting civilian infrastructure, while Moscow reports that a warehouse was hit.

entries.title: Thousands displaced by deadly Indonesia earthquake as rescue efforts continue
entries.snippet: Hundreds of homes and public buildings have been severely damaged with at least 51 people killed.

entries.title: Hurricane Lala lashes Hawaii with strong winds and torrential rain
entries.snippet: If the storm makes landfall, it will be Hawaii's first direct hit by a hurricane in 34 years.

entries.title: Twelve killed as Polish bus veers off Hungarian motorway
entries.snippet: Dozens more are seriously injured after the tourist bus overturned in the early hours of Sunday morning.

entries.title: Europe's tallest Virgin Mary statue unveiled in rural Poland
entries.snippet: The 55.6-metre (182ft) concrete figure is head-and-shoulders above Rio de Jaineiro's Christ the Redeemer.

entries.title: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to cross into Ceuta, reports say
entries.snippet: Security had been stepped up amid suggestions on social media of a second mass crossing on Saturday.

entries.title: Qatar denies capturing three Iranian pilots after downing fighter jets
entries.snippet: Iran claims they have been held since Qatar downed two fighter jets at the start of the US-Iran war.

entries.title: Liechtenstein changes succession rule to allow women to ascend the throne
entries.snippet: The declaration was made on the national day of the central European country, which has a population of just 44,000.

entries.title: Multiple suspects at large after five shot at Virginia State University, police say
entries.snippet: Police responded to reports of a shooting outside a residence halls at about 01:28 local time (05:28 GMT) on Saturday.

entries.title: Eleven killed in Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon, authorities say
entries.snippet: Israel's military said it had struck "Hezbollah terror infrastructure" in response to what it described as earlier action against its soldiers.

entries.title: Australian state to launch gun buyback after Bondi Beach attack
entries.snippet: New South Wales, where the attack took place, will offer gun owners cash to give up their firearms.

entries.title: Family stranded at sea for 16 hours after jet ski capsized in Thailand
entries.snippet: A father and his two young sons spent a night adrift before being rescued off the coast of the island of Koh Samui.

entries.title: BBC seeks to subpoena family members in Panorama lawsuit
entries.snippet: A spokesperson for Trump's legal team responded to the request accusing the broadcaster of "seeking to harass" the president's family.

entries.title: Firefighters battle wildfire tearing through Belgian nature reserve
entries.snippet: The fire burning through the major park was described as the country's worst in recent years.

entries.title: South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North
entries.snippet: Lee Jae Myung offers chance to end the conflict, which has been frozen since an armistice in 1953.

entries.title: France's top court blocks social media ban for under-15s
entries.snippet: The Constitutional Council says it infringes upon freedom of expression - but President Macron vows to prepare a new draft.

entries.title: US aircraft carrier on way to relieve USS Lincoln after issues reported aboard
entries.snippet: Thousands of sailors on the Lincoln have reportedly faced food shortages and broken plumbing, with some considering jumping overboard.

entries.title: Many Canadians are boycotting the US, so this is where they're travelling instead
entries.snippet: From exploring their own backyard to travelling abroad, many Canadians are spending their money elsewhere to send a message to the US president.

entries.title: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, does the West have any influence?
entries.snippet: Five years after the Taliban swept to power, many are asking whether the West has any bargaining chips left

entries.title: Secondhand book sales are booming. Is it because of AI?
entries.snippet: Booksellers are reporting mysterious bulk orders. It's thought the books are being used to train AI - and ending up pulped.

entries.title: As Trump blocks Medicaid funds, one trans teen's mom asks: What's next?
entries.snippet: A longtime Republican living in California says the Trump administration's continuing actions to target transgender youth take a personal toll.

entries.title: Ukraine launches one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, killing at least 6 people in Russia
entries.snippet: Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia Sunday, killing at least six people in one of Kyiv's largest aerial attacks of the war.

entries.title: NPR Senior Podcast Challenge: Official Rules
Doctors and women who've had it call for more attention on postpartum psychosis
entries.snippet: The high-profile murder trial of Lindsay Clancy's has put the condition in the spotlight. Women who have had it call for more research and understanding of a difficult mental illness.

entries.title: Billions of sea stars have died. A Northwest tribe is trying to save the species
entries.snippet: Sunflower sea stars are critically endangered in the Pacific Ocean. University of Washington researchers are working with the Samish Indian Nation to bring this 24-armed creature back from the brink of extinction.

entries.title: 65 and older? Have a story to tell? Hit 'record' and send NPR your podcast
entries.snippet: This fall, we're asking seniors to send us their stories in audio form. Our judges will pick the best ones and air them on NPR.

entries.title: Are robotaxis finally here?
entries.snippet: Fully self-driving cars for hire have been hailed as the technology of the future for years now. That future has finally arrived -- but only in some cities.

entries.title: State Department spokesperson on Iran war and U.S. visa revocations
entries.snippet: NPR's Rob Schmitz speaks with State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott about the with Iran and the hundreds of thousands of foreign nationals who have had their U.S. visa revoked.

entries.title: The Midwest braces for more heavy flooding, as Indiana seeks federal aid
entries.snippet: Indiana, Illinois and surrounding states are preparing for another stretch of flooding through this weekend.

entries.title: Families of USS Lincoln crew say Trump should be 'ashamed' of conditions on board
entries.snippet: President Trump said the USS Abraham Lincoln deployment is "not nearly long enough." A family member of a sailor on board that ship said those comments are shameful.

entries.title: Cyclospora spreads through human waste — so how did it get on food?
entries.snippet: The nationwide cyclospora outbreak is very likely a result of sewage contamination in the food supply, according to scientific researchers and public health officials.

entries.title: Indiana authorities say at least 5 people have died as severe weather crosses the state
entries.snippet: The state has been hammered over the past week by heavy rains, resulting in rivers reaching record levels and sending residents in search of higher ground.

entries.title: Democrats' 2028 presidential calendar gives Black and Latino voters and union members an early say
entries.snippet: The primary lineup pushes Iowa from the traditional top spot and makes South Carolina the leadoff state, voting on Jan. 22, 2028, followed by Nevada on Feb. 1.

entries.title: UK's leader calls for reflection after the death of former Cambridge professor accused of plagiarism
entries.snippet: Jason Arday, who became Cambridge's youngest Black professor in 2023, was found dead inside an address in south London on Friday.

entries.title: While Taliban leaders mark 5 years in power in Afghanistan, a UN official warns of a rights crisis
entries.snippet: The Taliban seized power on Aug. 15, 2021, as the U.S. and other NATO troops withdrew following a costly two-decade war. The U.S. withdrawal led to chaos at Kabul airport as crowds of people tried to flee the country in desperation.

entries.title: U.S. pulls last aircraft carrier in Asia as Trump focuses on Iran and the Western Hemisphere
entries.snippet: The USS George Washington is departing the Pacific and expected to replace the USS Abraham Lincoln in the Middle East amid growing concerns about mental health and supply issues aboard the long-deployed carrier.

entries.title: Israeli airstrikes on southern Lebanon kill 11 people in another test to truce
entries.snippet: Israel and the Lebanese government announced a "framework agreement" on June 26, laying out a plan for Israeli forces to withdraw from southern Lebanon in exchange for the disarmament of the Iran-backed Hezbollah militant group.

entries.title: Lala strengthens into a hurricane and bears down on Hawaii's Big Island with heavy rain, winds
entries.snippet: The National Hurricane Center said Lala's maximum sustained winds increased to 75 mph, making it a Category 1 hurricane.

entries.title: Magnitude 7.7 earthquake strikes off Indonesia's coast, killing at least 47 and toppling buildings
entries.snippet: Authorities issued a tsunami warning and urged coastal residents to move to higher ground, but later lifted the warning when Indonesia's meteorological agency said monitoring showed no significant sea-level changes that posed a threat to coastal communities.

entries.title: Army temporarily halts Apache helicopter training missions after deadly Texas crash
entries.snippet: No cause of the Wednesday crash has been released because the investigation has just begun. A safety investigation team from the Army Combat Readiness Center in Fort Rucker, Alabama, is trying to determine what happened, the Army said.

entries.title: Jason Arday, youngest Black professor at Cambridge, found dead at 41 after resignation
entries.snippet: A British sociologist who resigned last week from the University of Cambridge following weeks of public accusations of plagiarism and media scrutiny was found dead Friday.

entries.title: New aircraft carrier en route to Middle East after issues reported aboard USS Abraham Lincoln
entries.snippet: The Lincoln has been supporting the U.S. war against Iran, and its deployment has included a record-setting uninterrupted time at sea of more than 240 days.

entries.title: Luigi Mangione reveals motive for CEO's killing after pleading guilty in federal case
entries.snippet: In a surprise turn, Luigi Mangione pleaded guilty to the shooting death of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson. Mangione admitted he stalked and shot Thompson in 2024 outside a Hilton hotel in Manhattan. He potentially faces life in prison. The 28-year-old is also still facing st

entries.title: Trump dismisses concerns over conditions on long-deployed USS Abraham Lincoln
entries.snippet: Reports from sailors and their families describe concerning conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln. The ship has been at sea since last November, a record-length deployment. White House correspondent Liz Landers reports.

entries.title: Quick-thinking controller helps 2 planes with same flight number avoid possible disaster
entries.snippet: A potential disaster was averted Friday when a Phoenix air traffic controller recognized two American Airlines jets mistakenly were flying the same flight number and acted quickly to avoid confusion and keep them a safe distance apart.

entries.title: News Wrap: Record-breaking heat wave grips Europe
entries.snippet: In our news wrap Friday, a heat wave is breaking records across Europe, record-breaking rainfall triggered flooding across several cities in Japan, Hawaii is preparing for significant rain and strong winds from Tropical Storm Lala and authorities in Italy recovered a trio of stol

entries.title: Congo Ebola outbreak on track to become deadliest in history
entries.snippet: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to worsen, with the number of confirmed cases climbing to over 4,600. At least 2,100 people have died, a death toll that was reached almost three times faster than the outbreak over a decade ago. William Brangham di

entries.title: Greece toughens stance on illegal migration with new deportation plan
entries.snippet: Eleven years into a migration crisis, Greece is trying to stop boats crossing from North Africa to the Greek island of Crete. Five European Union countries have made a breakthrough in their efforts to deport migrants crossing the Mediterranean Sea. Uganda in East Africa has agree

entries.title: Brooks and Atkins Stohr on 'woke' politics in America
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Kimberly Atkins Stohr of the Boston Globe join William Brangham to discuss the week in politics, including the surprising result in Wisconsin's Democratic primary, the status of 'woke' politics in America and the stalemate between the U.S. and Ira

entries.title: Palestinians besieged in West Bank village of Qusra fear Israeli settlers will seize their homes
entries.snippet: The standoff in Qusra between Palestinian families and Israeli settlers who apparently want to push them out entered a new stage Friday as activists supporting the Palestinians marched toward the besieged homes to replenish their dwindling food and water supply.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Ukraine launches one of its largest attacks of war
entries.snippet: Russia says hundreds of drones targeted Moscow overnight, with six fatalities in the capital and southern Rostov region. Five people were killed in strikes across Ukraine.

entries.title: Bus crash in Hungary kills at least 12
entries.snippet: Police say they have arrested the driver of a bus that crashed in Hungary, killing at least 12 people. The bus was carrying Polish pilgrims, media report.

entries.title: Troops from North Korea to boost Russia's Ukraine forces
entries.snippet: Intelligence agencies report that North Korea is preparing to send up to 50,000 troops to Russia. But military experts doubt that this will make a fundamental difference in the course of Russia's war with Ukraine.

entries.title: US: Hurricane Lala brings Hawaii heavy rain, strong winds
entries.snippet: The Category 1 storm passed over Hawaii's Big Island without making landfall and is expected to weaken gradually. However, the hurricane caused roads to flood and turned rivers into raging torrents.

entries.title: Africa's low-key high-stakes Strait of Hormuz diplomacy
entries.snippet: African governments have kept a low profile on the international stage during the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz. But that doesn't mean they haven't been engaging with the issue behind the scenes.

entries.title: How Germany supports recovery of Berlin Pride attack victims
entries.snippet: After a terrorist attack, public attention tends to focus primarily on the perpetrator. But what about the victims? What support can they expect? And what lies ahead for them?

entries.title: Iran war: Qatar denies holding missing Iranian fighter pilots
entries.snippet: Tehran said the three pilots "were captured alive" by Qatari forces after their fighter jets were shot down in the early days of the US-Israel war with Iran. Qatar has denied Iran's claims.

entries.title: Morocco detains dozens of migrants trying to enter Spanish North African exclave Ceuta
entries.snippet: The attempted crossings come two weeks after around 72,000 people rushed into the Spanish North African exclave from Morocco. Calls for another mass crossing had been circulating on social media this week.

entries.title: Lebanon says 11 killed in Israeli airstrikes
entries.snippet: Lebanon's prime minister denounced the attacks on villages in southern Lebanon for targeting civilians in their homes. Israel said it was firing on Hezbollah infrastructure.

entries.title: Climate action doesn't seem to be a priority for Germany — despite heat-related deaths and drought. Why aren't more people taking to the streets?
entries.snippet: Climate action does not seem to be a priority for the German government — despite record temperatures, heat-related deaths and drought. Why aren't more people taking to the streets in protest?

entries.title: Hawaii under state of emergency ahead of historic hurricane
entries.snippet: A hurricane is forecast to hit the Big Island of Hawaii this weekend, bringing heavy rain and wind. Should it make landfall, Lala would be the first hurricane to hit the island since 1871.

entries.title: Russians snap up new homes built on Ukraine 'graveyard'
entries.snippet: Russia is constructing high-rises in the occupied Ukrainian city of Mariupol, on the sites of buildings it destroyed. Who's buying these properties? And what happened to the Ukrainians who used to lived here?

entries.title: Afghan allies still waiting for the safety Germany promised
entries.snippet: After the Taliban retook power on August 15, 2021, Berlin promised to bring Afghan staff to Germany. But people are still waiting to leave in Pakistan and Afghanistan.

entries.title: Trump's Latin America allies open arms to Israel
entries.snippet: While ongoing military actions in Gaza and settler attacks on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank have largely isolated Israel globally, Latin America's authoritarian right sees an opening for a strategic alliance.

entries.title: India: Modi promises free exam coaching, AI training for youth after protests
entries.snippet: Speaking on India's Independence Day, PM Modi announced free online coaching for competitive exams and AI training for 10 million youths, weeks after protests over alleged exam paper leaks and recruitment irregularities.

entries.title: Germany increasingly revokes refugee status for Syrians
entries.snippet: In the first half of 2026, 23.2% of reviews ended with protection being revoked or withdrawn, according to a government response to a parliamentary question by the socialist Left Party. DW has more.

entries.title: US: FDA recalls 19 million eggs over salmonella risk
entries.snippet: The US has issued a serious health warning over the recalled eggs, saying exposure to the potentially contaminated products could cause severe illness or death.

entries.title: Indonesia: Dozens dead after earthquake off Flores island
entries.snippet: At least 47 people have died and several buildings were damaged after the powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake, which was followed by dozens of aftershocks. A tsunami warning has been lifted.

entries.title: Donald Trump to declare Hormuz US territory 'soon'
entries.snippet: Donald Trump said the strait would become part of the US after Iran is defeated. He also told Americans to accept higher gas prices, which have soared since Iran closed Hormuz in response to US and Israeli attacks.
